messages:
maria: heads up — saw a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate for model gptx-13b on /chat/* routes starting ~02:00 UTC. Token-saved rate fell ~45k tokens/min at the trough. dashboard heatmap attached. anyone changed keying or seq boundaries?

aj: I noticed the same. correlates with the kernel-selector rollout at 02:55 (commit d4f1b). we changed sequence bucketing thresholds (seq_len_cutoff=256 -> 192) to try to favor smaller kernels. could that affect cache keys?

maria: that's my suspicion. the cache key includes truncated prefix length and seq boundary markers. if the selector changes how we chunk inputs, key normalization could diverge and blow the hit-rate.

sam: runtime-ci reports a deploy at 02:55: 
```
runtime-ci: deployed kernel-selector v2.3.1 to region-us-east-1 (d4f1b) — rollout 100%
```

aj: confirmed. also the batching heuristics update earlier that hour may have altered how we group small requests into batches, which can change prefix truncation at the edge. two moving pieces.

jules: quick sanity checks i ran:
- promql: `sum(rate(prefix_cache.hit_tokens_total[5m])) by (model,route,tenant) / sum(rate(prefix_cache.request_tokens_total[5m])) by (model,route,tenant)` shows gptx-13b:/chat drop from 0.72 -> 0.18 at 02:00–03:00 UTC.
- key-entropy: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(prefix_cache_key_entropy_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))` spiked for gptx-13b.

maria: nice. can we produce a per-tenant top-10 churn list and a key-diff sample? i want to see exact key strings for hits vs misses for a random seed of requests.

aj: i'll add a dashboard panel: rows = model, cols = route, cells = hit-rate; sidebars = top-ten tenants by token-saved delta. also add a table that shows example request->cache-key transformations for hits vs misses.

sam: proposed alert: sustained 5m hit-rate < 0.35 AND tokens-saved drop > 20k/min for any model+route -> severity=high. route to eng-runtime oncall.

jules: idea: we may be leaking seq boundary flags into the key when the batcher splits messages mid-turn. i can run a small profiler to capture the exact code path: record at key-gen entry with (model, route, trunc_len, seq_markers, kernel_bucket).

maria: please run that and dump 1k samples. if keys differ only by trunc_len or seq_marker, we should normalize key builder to strip those transient artifacts or canonicalize chunking borders.

aj: temporary mitigation: we can enable prefix-warmup (prefetch cached prefixes) for top 5 tenants on gptx-13b to reduce cold penalty while we fix keying. warmup policy: prefetch on first 2 requests in 10s window.

sam: action items:
- aj: add dashboard panels + alert (ETA 45m)
- jules: capture key-gen traces + 1k samples (ETA 30m)
- runtime-ci: rollback toggle for kernel-selector if root cause traced to rollout (ready)
- maria: coordinate with customer success if top tenants affected (I'll start on comms)

runtime-ci: rollback toggle is set to v2.2 (safe) and can be flipped with `./rollout toggle kernel-selector v2.2` — advise before flipping.

jules: quick dump finds most misses differ only in `seq_marker=1` vs `seq_marker=0` when batcher splits after punctuation. patch idea: normalize seq_marker in key when route is stateless (chat routes are stateless for caching).

maria: good find. prioritize a fix to key normalization + add unit test for seq boundary symmetry. after that, re-run the dashboard and measure token-saved recovery.

aj: i'll also add a heatmap panel of key-entropy over time per-model so we can catch this class of regressions earlier.

sam: adding runbook note: if hit-rate drops >40% and token-saved delta >30k, escalate to eng-ml and consider immediate rollback.

maria: summary: probable regression from kernel-selector + batcher interacting to change seq-boundary keying. next 90m plan: dashboards+alerts (aj), traces+samples (jules), optional rollback ready (runtime-ci), comms (maria). i'll post back with token-saved recovery after fixes. :thumbsup:
